title: Graders never see the writer's receipts: independent grading isolation
description:
What: enforce grader isolation - the grading agent receives the packet and sources, never the writer's self-report, scores, or receipts; grading receipts record the isolation.
Why: self-graded work is how a 9.57 hid six deleted trigger phrases in the skills program; the same failure mode applies to packets.
Origin: reality-check phase 2; skills-program lesson (score is a false hope).
acceptance_criteria: Grading harness shows grader inputs exclude writer artifacts (logged manifest); a re-grade of one packet under isolation matches or explains differences vs its original grade; receipts cite the isolation manifest hash.

title: Review, validate and publish the living research loop

title: EPIC: one operating discipline across missions and agents
description:

Why: two missions (franken, skill library) share one fleet, one Mac, and one operator; discipline that lives in one mission's habits does not protect the other.

title: EPIC: the nightly operating loop runs itself end to end
description:

Why: reality check 2026-10-03: the loop shipped once with manual completion (PR #20) and once evaluator-green but gate-blocked. It is not yet self-sustaining.

acceptance_criteria: Epic closes when fr-nightly-proof-week closes on 7 consecutive launchd nights with zero manual repo writes and every child bead is closed on cited evidence.

title: Morning reports still land when the VM cron worker dies on provider overload
description: What: the 07:20 franken-nightly report job (VM cron) failed 2026-10-03 on provider overload (529/engine_overloaded) before reading the Mac state; the report only reached Josh because an agent checked the Mac by hand. AGENTS.md records cron workers dying twice before. Make the report path resilient: the Mac driver already writes state/last-run.json and state/<date>-report.md; the delivery step needs a design that survives a dead reader (Mac-side digest artifact + thinner reader, or a local notifier).\nWhy: a nightly that silently goes unreported reads as a failed night; Josh should never have to ask whether it ran.\nOrigin: cron run e438c26f 2026-10-03 provider overload; prior cron deaths 2026-10-02.
acceptance_criteria: A report reaches Josh for a simulated dead-worker morning without manual recovery: evidence is a delivered digest produced from Mac artifacts (state/last-run.json + report.md) even when the VM reader turn fails; mechanism documented in RUNBOOK.md.
